_status: READ FROM CHARTS BY EYE (pixel measurement of slides 9 and 10, 6U blue line). Uncertainty about +/-0.1 yr at 430 km and +/-0.15 yr at 550 km. Not official DAS output. Do not edit values except by re-reading the deck.

source.title: Variation in Predicted Orbital Lifetime Due to Launch Year
source.author: Caley Burke, NASA Launch Services Program (KSC)

das_inputs_from_slide_19.solar_flux_data: F10 release dated 2023-09-27 (a PREDICTION, not the real Sun)
das_inputs_from_slide_19.altitude: 'Perigee altitude' 430 km (slide 19) and 550 km (slide 20); whether the orbit is circular is not stated on the slide
das_inputs_from_slide_19.launch_date_within_year: NOT STATED on the slides; the x axis is Launch Year (one point per year, 2021 to 2044)
das_inputs_from_slide_19.slide_20_inputs: slide 20 inputs not read yet; assumed identical except altitude

spacecraft.note: ballistic coefficient implied by Cd 2.2: Cd*A/m = 0.0154 m2/kg, i.e. m/(Cd*A) = 64.9 kg/m2

caveats: DAS used a Sept 2023 solar-flux PREDICTION for every year. Our truth mode uses the real Sun through Oct 2026. So launch years 2021 to 2026 are NOT a like-for-like comparison: real Cycle 25 peaked higher than the 2023 prediction.
Launch years 2027 and later use a prediction on both sides (ours: NASA Oct 2026 prediction; theirs: Sept 2023). These are the fairest points for a pass/fail check.
Inclination is 51.6 deg (ISS-type), so use our 51.6 deg density table, not the SSO table.
The deck's 'launch year' start date inside the year is unknown. Test with the same date for all years (say 1 Jan) and disclose; do not tune it to pass.
The 550 km curve has a jump between 2033 and 2034 (6.85 to 9.58 years): it is in the deck, not a reading error.

test_definition.name: golden 2
test_definition.informational_points: launch years 2021-2026 (different Sun); report the ratio but do not fail
shape_checks: the 430 km lifetime peaks near 2029-2030 and 2040 and is lowest near 2035
the 550 km lifetime has its sharp rise between launch years 2033 and 2034
lifetime at 550 km is always longer than at 430 km for the same launch year
test_definition.never: No parameter fitting to pass this test. If it fails, disclose the ratio in README and keep the test.
